html:
Guayabo is an ancient town on the slopes of Turrialba volcano in central Costa Rica, at its height from about 800 to 1200 CE and abandoned before the Spanish came.

Its builders laid out round house mounds, paved causeways and stone-lined channels that carried water to tanks. Some channels still carry water today. Petroglyphs are cut into boulders around the site. At its peak it may have housed a few thousand people under a chief.

It was explored from the late 1800s and made a national monument in 1973. It is the largest excavated site in Costa Rica and shows a way of life very different from the stone cities of the Maya to the north. The stone spheres of the south come from a related world of chiefdoms that the Spanish conquest swept away.
sum: Guayabo is an ancient town on the slopes of Turrialba volcano in central Costa Rica, at its height from about 800 to 1200 CE and abandoned before the Spanish came.
